long_biography.plain_text:
Interamerican made Dimitris Kontominas a defining figure in modern Greek insurance. He co-founded the life insurer in 1969 after working at Alico, developed it into the country's market leader and sold his controlling stake to Eureko in 2001. The transaction crystallised the value of a company he had led for more than three decades.

Kontominas repeatedly redeployed capital into new sectors. He founded banks, acquired television and cinema businesses, and created private clinics, producing an unusually broad Greek portfolio. Even so, insurance retained institutional importance: he later chaired the Hellenic Association of Insurance Companies and was named its honorary president.
